data.narrative:
Canada Rocket Company is a Seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Hugh Kolias and David Tenny. The company has raised $6.2M to date. The broader Space & Aerospace sector includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers, though none at an equivalent stage and scale for narrow-set median benchmarking.

Of the three valuation methods examined, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. Using the $6.2M total raised as a base proxy for Seed-stage value and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next funding stage yields an implied valuation of $15.5M. Peer-median analysis was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables in the Space & Aerospace universe. Public-comp anchoring could not be executed because the target company does not disclose revenue, a prerequisite for price-to-sales multiples (sector median: 26.4x across 5 public tickers).

The analysis supports a valuation range of $13M to $18M, with a midpoint of $16M. This range reflects a ±15% sensitivity around the Stage-Progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of peer-benchmarked validation and lack of revenue visibility; a future funding round or disclosed financial metrics would improve precision and enable multi-method triangulation.
